questions.question: To join the internet, the computer has to be connected to an
questions.explanation: A computer joins the internet through an Internet Service Provider. The IAB and Internet Society are standards/governance bodies.

questions.question: In BFS, vertices are explored level by level, starting from the:
questions.explanation: BFS starts at the source (level 0, the shallowest level) and explores all vertices at distance 1, then 2, and so on. Going deep first is DFS.

questions.question: Frame design in the Data Link Layer includes:

options.A: Deciding the routing path for data packets
options.B: Defining the structure of data frames

questions.explanation: Framing in the data link layer defines how bits are grouped into frames, including headers, trailers and delimiters. Routing and IP addressing belong to the network layer.

questions.question: Which command is used to remove a relation from an SQL database?
questions.explanation: DROP TABLE removes the relation together with its structure from the database. DELETE only removes rows and keeps the table; REMOVE is not an SQL command.

questions.question: Telnet is commonly used for:
questions.explanation: Telnet provides remote terminal (command-line) access to another host. It is insecure, so secure transfers and remote logins use SFTP/SSH instead.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of interrupt?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Interrupts are classified as hardware and software interrupts (plus exceptions/traps). Memory interrupt is not a standard interrupt type.

questions.question: In EDI, I stands for?
questions.explanation: EDI stands for Electronic Data Interchange: computer-to-computer exchange of business documents in a standard format.

questions.question: Chief component of first generation computer was
questions.explanation: First generation computers (1940s-1950s) used vacuum tubes (valves). Transistors came in the second generation and ICs in the third.

questions.question: .......... is a device that forwards packets between networks by processing the routing information included in the packet.
questions.explanation: A router forwards packets between networks using the routing (IP) information in the packet. A bridge works within a LAN at the data link layer.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a step in the Divide and Conquer algorithm?
questions.explanation: Divide and conquer has three steps: Divide, Conquer and Combine. All three listed options are steps, so none of them is NOT a step.

questions.question: How can one implement the compile-time polymorphism in the C++ programming language?

options.B: By using the concepts of inheritance
options.C: By using both the virtual functions and inheritance
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Templates (like function overloading) are resolved by the compiler, giving compile-time polymorphism. Virtual functions with inheritance give runtime polymorphism.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a limitation of file system?
questions.explanation: Traditional file systems suffer from data redundancy, inconsistency and program-data dependence. Storing space is not a listed limitation of a file system; it is simply a resource.

questions.question: Connected components in a graph can be found using which graph traversal algorithm?
questions.explanation: Starting a traversal from each unvisited vertex marks one whole connected component, and this works equally with DFS or BFS. Choosing only DFS ignores that BFS visits exactly the same reachable set.

questions.question: Which testing approach involves testing individual components or units of code?
questions.explanation: Unit testing checks individual components or units of code in isolation. Integration testing checks interactions between units.

questions.question: In binary subtraction using the simple method, if a borrow is needed from a digit and the borrowed digit is 1, what happens to the next digit's value?
questions.explanation: When a borrow is taken from a digit that is 1, that digit is decremented by 1 (becoming 0) and the current position gets 2 (binary 10).

questions.question: ASCII and EBCDIC are the popular character coding systems. What does EBCDIC stand for?

options.A: Extended Binary Coded Decimal Interchange Code
options.B: Extended Bit Code Decimal Interchange Code
options.C: Extended Bit Case Decimal Interchange Code
options.D: Extended Binary Case Decimal Interchange Code

questions.explanation: EBCDIC is Extended Binary Coded Decimal Interchange Code, an 8-bit code used by IBM mainframes.

questions.question: What does the acronym "HTTP" stand for?
questions.explanation: HTTP stands for HyperText Transfer Protocol, the application-layer protocol for transferring web pages.

questions.question: Which characteristics are taken together in chromaticity?
questions.explanation: Chromaticity specifies colour quality independent of luminance, i.e. hue and saturation taken together. Adding brightness gives the full colour description.

questions.question: What does a first order predicate logic contain?
questions.explanation: A sentence in first-order predicate logic consists of a predicate and the subject(s) (terms/objects) it applies to, e.g. Man(Socrates).

questions.question: What does I stand for in CIA?
questions.explanation: The CIA triad of information security is Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability; I stands for Integrity.

questions.question: What is a database?

options.A: Organized collection of information that cannot be accessed, updated and managed
options.B: Organized collection of data or information that can be accessed, updated and managed
options.C: Organized collection of data that cannot be updated
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A database is an organized collection of data or information that can be easily accessed, updated and managed.

questions.question: In OOP, which term refers to a mechanism by which a class can inherit properties and behaviors from another class?
questions.explanation: Inheritance is the mechanism by which a class acquires properties and behaviours of another class. Polymorphism is one interface with many forms, and encapsulation is bundling data with methods.

questions.question: Thread shares with other threads belonging to the same process its

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Threads of the same process share the code section, data section and OS resources such as open files. Each thread has its own thread ID, program counter, registers and stack.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an NP-Complete problem?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The shortest path problem is solvable in polynomial time (e.g. Dijkstra), so it is in P and is not NP-complete. TSP (decision version) and SAT are NP-complete.

questions.question: The maximum length (in bytes) of an IPv4 datagram is:
questions.explanation: The IPv4 Total Length field is 16 bits, so the largest datagram is 2^16 - 1 = 65535 bytes including the header.
